741116595.accepts_evidence: The guidelines say applications are accepted at any time on the foundation's own form, one per applicant per fiscal year (https://www.edrachal.org/grant-guidelines/)
741116595.deadlines: rolling (accepted at any time; no deadline)
741116595.eligibility: 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organizations or governmental entities. One application per applicant per fiscal year (September 1 to August 31). The contact person must hold an official position with the applicant, not be a contractor or outside grant writer.
741116595.geographic_limits: Texas only; all grant funds must be spent within Texas
741116595.grant_range_stated: not stated (no minimum or maximum; the foundation may award a different amount than requested)
741116595.how_to_apply: Complete the foundation's Grant Application Form with Exhibits A to E (IRS letter, latest tax return and financial statements, corporate documents and board list, other funding requests, any relationships with foundation directors) and email it as one PDF to info@edrachal.org.
741116595.name: Ed Rachal Foundation
741116595.notes: The guidelines warn that requests far exceed available funds and only a small share is approved; awards are announced by mail and the board approves every grant. Grant writers cannot be the listed contact. The application page advises against using Chrome because of PDF-saving problems. Public announcements of a grant need the foundation's prior approval.
741116595.page_dated: Footer copyright 2023; application form file dated November 2016
priorities: Charitable, scientific, literary or educational purposes benefiting Texas (no narrower focus areas are named)
741116595.types_of_support: The form gives general operating funds, capital campaign, scholarship assistance or a named project as examples

741403105.accepts_evidence: Eligible organizations may send a grant inquiry through the online portal at any time; staff then invite a full application if the inquiry advances. https://moodyf.org/application-process
741403105.contact: The Moody Foundation, 2302 Post Office St. #704, Galveston, TX 77550; (409) 797-1500. M-Pact Fund: Courtney Rogers, Vice President, Education; Angela Blair, Director, Education.
741403105.deadlines: Rolling for general inquiries; trustees meet four times a year (dates not given); inquiry to decision can take up to six months. Education M-Pact Fund Cycle 4 (rural) is by invitation: nominations July 2025, planning grants November 2025, implementation awards May 2026.
741403105.eligibility: Eligible Texas organizations that pass a short eligibility quiz in the portal (details are in a Grant FAQ not read). M-Pact Fund: 501(c)(3) nonprofits or public entities; the current cycle is limited to rural Texas communities.
741403105.geographic_limits: Texas only; funds must be spent in and benefit Texas.
741403105.how_to_apply: Take the eligibility quiz and submit a grant inquiry (project description, total budget, amount requested) in the Grants Portal; wait for staff to send the full application.
741403105.name: The Moody Foundation
741403105.not_funded: Not stated beyond process limits: one inquiry at a time, one active grant at a time, and no new inquiry from a grantee until the prior final report is in (unless staff agree).
741403105.notes: Two tracks: the general inquiry route (open year-round) and the Education M-Pact Fund, whose current fourth cycle is rural-only and invitation-only. The November 30 date on the tax return is for the scholarship program, not grants. A national organization would need a Texas project and Texas spending.
741403105.page_dated: Application process page modified April 24, 2025; M-Pact page modified August 29, 2025; copyright 2026
priorities: Education M-Pact Fund: early learning and postsecondary success
741403105.types_of_support: Project requests (applicant gives total project budget and amount sought); other types not stated.

742158821.accepts_evidence: Only invited proposals are reviewed, but any nonprofit may send an Initial Inquiry through an online form; staff reply within six weeks and may invite a concept paper, then a proposal. https://greatertexasfoundation.org/grants/grant-application-review/
742158821.conflicts_with_return: Return says preselected only; the site offers an open Initial Inquiry form, though full proposals are by invitation.
742158821.deadlines: No deadlines; inquiries answered within six weeks; proposal review usually takes two months or more.
742158821.eligibility: Nonprofit organizations only; a college or university unit or department may apply.
742158821.geographic_limits: Texas students; no narrower boundary stated.
742158821.how_to_apply: Submit the Initial Inquiry form (organization and contact details plus a 300-word project description). If invited, file a concept paper and then a full proposal in the online application system.
742158821.name: Greater Texas Foundation
742158821.not_funded: Individuals and businesses. Generally one application per organization (or university unit) in twelve months; declined ideas should not come back without real revision; past grantees need a timely expenditure report first.
742158821.notes: Postsecondary-focused. Recent grantees listed are mostly universities, community colleges, research groups and intermediaries, so a K-12 financial literacy or work-readiness program would need a clear line to college or career pathways. Favors broad reach and measurable impact under its strategic plan.
742158821.page_dated: Application page published June 11, 2021, last modified November 13, 2025
priorities: Postsecondary access, persistence and completion for Texas students

743052411.accepts_evidence: Site says unsolicited requests are not accepted; a nonprofit must be invited by a Cathay Bank or Foundation officer, who supplies a link for a letter of intent. https://www.cathaybank.com/cathay-foundation/application-guidelines
743052411.conflicts_with_return: none - return says preselected only and the site says invitation only. The return lists a contact (Nancy Tarr) that the site pages read do not show.
743052411.contact: No named grants contact shown on the pages read (email is hidden on the page); general contact page cathaybank.com/contact-us
743052411.deadlines: No deadlines listed; the board reviews requests quarterly.
743052411.eligibility: IRS-recognized 501(c)(3) nonprofits serving Cathay Bank communities, invited by a bank or foundation officer. Applicants report the share of clients who are low- or moderate-income.
743052411.geographic_limits: Communities in the Cathay Bank service network: California, Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts, Nevada, New York, New Jersey, Texas and Washington. Organizations serving areas outside the bank's communities are ineligible.
743052411.grant_range_stated: New applicants receive no more than $5,000. No other range given.
743052411.how_to_apply: Obtain an invitation from a Cathay Bank or Foundation officer, submit a letter of intent through the link the officer provides, and submit a full application if invited (cover letter, two years of budgets and audits or 990s, board list, major funders).
743052411.name: Cathay Bank Foundation
743052411.not_funded: Unsolicited grant proposals and sponsorship requests are declined; requests outside the focus areas or outside the bank's operating areas are unlikely to be funded.
743052411.notes: The route in is a relationship with a local Cathay Bank officer. Texas is in the service area. The foundation also runs a scholarship program, not read.
priorities: community and economic development (affordable housing, home-buyer counseling, small business and jobs, workforce and life skills)
education (academic support for low- and moderate-income youth, financial literacy, mentoring, ESL, entrepreneurship)
health and welfare (shelters, food banks, services for at-risk children and families, mental health, health education)
organizations where more than half of those served are low- or moderate-income

746036466.accepts_evidence: Every new applicant must submit a short pre-application during a set monthly window; full proposals are by invitation after that. https://www.brownfoundation.org/grant-seekers/
746036466.conflicts_with_return: Minor: return lists bfi@brownfoundation.org and Ann Ziker as contact; the site gives grants@brownfoundation.org.
746036466.deadlines: Pre-application windows: Cycle 1 May 1-31, 2026; Cycle 2 July 1-31, 2026; Cycle 3 October 1-31, 2026; Cycle 4 January 1-31, 2027. Submissions outside a window are held for the next one.
746036466.eligibility: 501(c)(3) public charities. Most grantees are at growth or maturity stage with evidence of results, serve at least about 1,000 people a year (or are scaling to that), and have operating budgets over $1 million.
746036466.geographic_limits: Greater Houston, mainly Harris County; Montgomery, Fort Bend, Brazoria and Galveston counties occasionally. Requests from outside greater Houston are rarely approved.
746036466.grant_range_stated: not stated; size depends on the organization's scale, maturity, prior relationship and program area
746036466.how_to_apply: Submit the online pre-application (no login needed) in an open window; expect word in roughly 2 to 4 weeks after the window closes. If invited, create a Grantee Community login and file the full proposal within about a month.
746036466.name: The Brown Foundation, Inc.
746036466.not_funded: 509(a)(3) supporting organizations, Type III organizations and private operating foundations; endowments and endowment campaigns; debt retirement; event sponsorships and galas; approaches made through consultants. Start-ups without a proof point are not typically funded.
746036466.notes: Next window is January 1-31, 2027. A declined organization may reapply once per fiscal year (July 1 to June 30) and gets no individual feedback. Whole process takes at least three months. The foundation wants direct contact with senior leadership, not consultants. A Fort Worth applicant is outside the stated geography.
746036466.page_dated: Cycle dates for 2026 and January 2027; copyright 2026; guiding principles refer to 2025 grantmaking
746036466.types_of_support: General operating support, program support, capital projects and campaigns.

746070484.conflicts_with_return: None. Return shows no deadlines or restrictions; site adds a Texas preference and the one-request-per-year rule.
746070484.contact: 713-681-7868; 6131 Westview Drive, Houston, TX 77055 (email is on the page but hidden from automated readers)
746070484.deadlines: Rolling; no deadlines. Board reviews quarterly.
746070484.eligibility: Qualified nonprofit organizations only. One request per organization in any twelve-month period.
746070484.geographic_limits: Preference for organizations in the Houston area or elsewhere in Texas.
746070484.how_to_apply: Apply online through the foundation's YourCause portal (the old system closed 23 December 2025; unfinished applications there must be restarted). Receipt and status updates come by email and the portal dashboard.
746070484.name: Albert & Ethel Herzstein Charitable Foundation
746070484.not_funded: Individuals. Lobbying individual directors can hurt an application.
746070484.notes: Mission language is explicitly values-driven (Judeo-Christian beliefs and American values such as free enterprise and self-sufficiency); a JA-style financial literacy and enterprise pitch should speak to those words.
746070484.page_dated: Footer copyright 2026; page metadata modified 2026-07-09; new portal as of late December 2025.
priorities: Stated values: free enterprise, limited government, individual freedom, equal opportunity, self-sufficiency, hard work, resourcefulness
746070484.types_of_support: Not listed by type; the page mentions grants toward capital campaigns and endowments, each with its own final-report form.
